This Ashben Conversions Camper Van Is a Head-Turner Outside and a Refined Retreat Inside
16 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions
It's incredible what some specialized camper van builders can do when working with the limited interior real estate offered by vans. Thanks to efficient, clever designs, a camper van can be almost as well-equipped as a tiny studio apartment – take this rig as an example.
What we have here is a conversion based on a MAN TGE. It was created by Ashben Conversions, a Sheffield, UK-based company specializing in high-quality camper vans and motorhomes.
This rig was built by Ashben as a ready-to-go inventory van, and was sold completed to a customer who was able to skip the conversion wait list. As always, let's begin by taking a look at the exterior.
For starters, the vehicle is a head-turner thanks to its exterior look. It's finished in Crayon Grey paint and has several black exterior mods , as well as a small black decal with white geometric lines.
The vehicle rides on 20-inch Riviera wheels wrapped in General Grabber all-terrain tires. On top of the rig, Ashben fitted a Thule 6300 awning, a Heki roof vent, two Maxxair vent fans, and a 250 W solar panel.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions Other notable mods include power and water hookups, an outdoor shower connection, an access door for the toilet waste, and a set of flares.
Flares, also known as pods or capsules, are designed to increase the van width to allow you to arrange a bed inside east to west instead of the standard north to south. This rig's CJL side pods are color matched to the van's paint and come with half-slider windows.
Inside is where things get interesting. You'll be greeted by a modern, well-crafted interior with a variety of comforts. It has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space.
Regarding aesthetics, you'll notice cabinetry with a darker grain finish, grey Alcantara upholstery for the walls, and a ceiling finished in grey woven fabric, complete with three long recessed LED light strips. The look is complemented by white solid surface countertops and a variety of black accents, such as black leather upholstery and black hardware.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions The driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, allowing you to turn them around to face the back of the van. The front part of the interior can double as a seating area for after you set up camp, especially since you get a table that can be reached from either seat.
The seating area continues further back in the form of a dual bench seat complete with seat belts. There's also a cabinet above offering a decent amount of storage space.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side, by the sliding door. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a cover, a single-burner induction stovetop, a microwave oven, and a fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
A sizeable overhead cabinet, four drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage in the kitchen.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions Most high-end camper vans come with one of the most sought-after camper van facilities: a bathroom. This van's bathroom sits opposite the kitchen, hidden behind a tall standard door.
It boasts a stainless steel tray, a bench toilet that can be emptied from the outside, and a shower with a handheld wand. I'm also fond of the bathroom's look, with a concrete effect paired with black fixtures.
The rear part of the living space is taken up by a fixed sleeping arrangement with a double-sized bed that's 6'4" (193 centimeters) long. The bedroom also offers a Maxxair vent fan above, two overhead cabinets, two reading lights, and a small open cupboard.
Finally, we have the garage underneath the bedroom, accessible from both inside and outside the van. It provides abundant room for storage and accommodates part of the utility systems inside two boxes on the sides.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions The builders installed gas struts, which make it easier for you to open the rear doors and prevent them from slamming shut or hitting the vehicle's body.
Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 460 Ah Fogstar battery bank and a 3,000 W Victron inverter/charger. Three charging sources are available: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running. If you use them correctly, you might just never run out of juice while traveling.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 10-liter (2.6-gallon) Propex water heater and two tanks for fresh and grey water – both are mounted underneath the vehicle.
The last important system in this rig is a diesel-powered Webasto heater that's tapped directly into the vehicle's fuel tank.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Ashben Conversions All in all, Ashben Conversions created a comfortable and travel-ready mobile home with an enviable blend of practicality and aesthetics. Unfortunately, we don't know how much this van cost, but the company offers a configurator that lets you easily customize your dream build and find out a price estimate for it.
